title: Vayigash: don't fall out on the way (Genesis 45:24)
hookLine: Joseph sends his brothers home: "See that ye fall not out by the way"
carry: don't fall out on the way

lines: WHAT NOBODY SAID IN THE ROOM.
cards: Some family car rides go like this. The wedding is over, or the funeral, or the big talk, and now everyone's in the car together for three hours, and all the things nobody said in the room are sitting in the back seat.
Joseph's brothers are about to take that ride. They've just learned the brother they sold is alive and running Egypt. They're loaded with grain and gifts, heading home to tell their father.
And somebody, at some point on that road, is going to say: this was your idea.

teach.b: Joseph sees it coming. He loads them with wagons and food. He gives each brother a change of clothes, and Benjamin, pointedly, three hundred pieces of silver and five changes.
Then, at the door, one line. In the old Jewish Publication Society translation: "See that ye fall not out by the way." In Hebrew, al tirgezu ba-derech: don't get stirred up on the road.
Rashi, the medieval commentator, says: don't quarrel about me. Don't spend the trip arguing over who said sell him and who went along. The past is settled; don't reopen it on the highway.

teach.h: DON'T GET LOST ON THE ROAD.
teach.b: The Talmud offers a funnier, gentler reading: don't get so deep into a Torah argument on the road that you miss your turn. And take normal steps, and get into town before dark.
Practical travel advice from a brother who knows the route. A third reader, Rashbam, hears the verb differently.

teach.h: DON'T BE AFRAID ON THE WAY.
teach.b: It can mean to tremble, so he reads it as: don't be afraid on the way. You're not in trouble anymore. And the Talmud raises one more eyebrow, at those five sets of clothes for Benjamin.
Didn't one special coat start this whole disaster? The sages ask the question honestly. Put the readings together: the fight's over.

teach.h: DON'T FALL OUT ON THE WAY.
teach.b: Don't restart it, don't get lost in it, and don't carry the fear home with you.

how: Jews traditionally say the traveler's prayer, Tefillat HaDerech, when setting out on a journey beyond their town, asking for a safe road and a peaceful return.

o: go in peace, Joseph's farewell to his brothers
he sent away, the portion where Noah sends the dove
he came close, the portion where Joseph forgives

games.q: three readings of one line — tap the pairs.
p: don't get lost in a debate on the road
don't be afraid on the way

s: Joseph gave every brother exactly the same gifts
each got a change of clothes; Benjamin got five, and three hundred pieces of silver.
the Hebrew verb can mean to be stirred up with anger or with fear
that's why Rashi reads quarreling and Rashbam reads being afraid.
the Talmud notices the extra gifts to Benjamin
the sages ask how Joseph could favor one brother after one special coat caused so much harm.

games.q: you're Joseph. your brothers are loaded up and about to leave for a long trip home together. what's your last word?
o: remind them what they did to you.
tell them not to fall out on the way.
send a guard to keep an eye on them.
games.why: Joseph said: see that ye fall not out by the way. Rashi reads it as: don't quarrel about who sold me.

practice: Think of the next time you'll be on the move with someone: a commute, a school run, a walk, a long call, even a group chat.
If an old argument is waiting to ride along, picture it getting in the car, then picture yourself leaving it at the curb. Decide one thing you won't bring up on this trip.

wordCard.voice: Vayigash. The portion where Joseph, forgiving his brothers, sends them home with wagons and one warning: don't fight on the road.

orig.note: Hebrew: don't be stirred up on the road. Joseph's parting words (Genesis 45:24).

carryVoice: Your line: don't fall out on the way. Forgiven in the room, and still forgiven on the road. Tomorrow, the wagons arrive.

sources.q: See that ye fall not out by the way.
